records.quote: A man who has committed a murder with a revolver which he found on the spot would fling it away at once; he would not carry it up to London with him.
records.paraphrase: Poirot uses deductive reasoning about likely behavior to identify a flaw in the criminals' plan.

records.quote: Dumfounded, I took the wire to Japp. He swore softly under his breath.
records.paraphrase: The narrator and Japp react with astonishment to Poirot's instruction to arrest the housekeeper.

records.quote: In detective-novels, clues abound, but here I could find nothing that struck me as out of the ordinary except a large bloodstain on the carpet
records.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts fictional detective stories with the sparse evidence he finds in reality.

records.quote: You should know my methods by now. All I ask is that you should report to me fully every day, and follow implicitly any instructions I may wire you.
records.paraphrase: Poirot describes a systematic method of remote investigation through daily reports and instructions.

records.quote: His face, however, was haggard, and he was evidently laboring under great agitation.
records.paraphrase: Havering appears distressed and agitated when seeking help.

records.quote: The bullet had been extracted and was proved to have been fired from a revolver identical in size to the one held by the police.
records.paraphrase: Forensic examination of the bullet establishes the type of weapon used.

records.quote: I examined everything with painstaking care and took a couple of pictures of the room with my little camera, which I had brought with me. I also examined the ground outside the window
records.paraphrase: The narrator conducts a careful physical examination of the crime scene and photographs it.

records.quote: let us examine the facts methodically and in order.
records.paraphrase: Poirot proposes a methodical, ordered analysis of the facts to reach the solution.

records.quote: It is suggested that the reader pause in his perusal of the story at this point, make his own solution of the mystery\u2014and then see how close he comes to that of the author
records.paraphrase: An editorial note directly addresses the reader, inviting them to solve the mystery.

criteria.rationale: This is a classic detective mystery with no scientific facts, theories, discoveries, or speculative sciences materially represented.

Only ordinary contemporary items appear (revolvers, camera, railway, telegrams). None is a speculative invention or engineered system driving the setting or outcome; these are ordinary tools of the period.
The story is set in an ordinary contemporary present with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.
No consequences are developed from an identifiable scientific, technological, social, or historical premise; the narrative is a self-contained crime plot.

Understanding is materially driven by systematic inference: forensic bullet analysis establishes the weapon, physical crime-scene examination is conducted, and Poirot explicitly proposes methodical ordered analysis of facts and deduces the flaw in the plan through evidence-based reasoning. This exceeds mere generic question-asking.
No other planets, dimensions, or nonordinary cosmic environments or visitors appear; settings are ordinary English locations.
A single murder and an air crash killing two people are personal misfortunes, not a large-scale natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused disaster.

candidates.description: Poirot's method of solving the murder remotely from his sickbed via daily telegraphed reports and instructions, relying purely on ratiocination.

novelty.rationale: Remote armchair detection by deductive reasoning is fully consonant with the empirical norm of the classic detective genre; it introduces no totalizing or world-altering difference from the author's empirical world. It is a method, not a new ontological condition of the storyworld.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The detection is presented as a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural procedure grounded in behavioral inference and forensic reasoning. However this cognitive coherence does not rescue the absent novelty.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: Poirot's deductive method structures the entire narrative logic and its resolution, including the reader challenge. But centrality alone cannot compensate for absent novelty.

estrangement.rationale: The narrator explicitly contrasts detective-novel expectations with the sparse reality he confronts, and the editorial note invites the reader to compete with the detective, producing a mild cognitive-play estrangement rather than a world-altering novum.
